phrases.text: So
welcome back again.
It's time to solve one more problem. Now, in this problem, we are given that a train is two hundred meters long and it is running at fifty-four kilometers per hour.
The train crosses a platform in thirty seconds.
The question is asking us to find the length of the platform.
Now, the important words here are,
"crosses a platform."
What does this actually mean?
When a train crosses a platform,
it does not cover only the platform.
The entire train has to enter the platform and then completely come out of it.
So the total distance covered is length of the train plus length of the platform.
This is the basic concept to remember.
Now, let us assume the length of the platform is
x meter.
Before using the formula, let us convert the speed into meter per second.
Fifty-four multiplied by five divided by eighteen gives us fifteen meter per second.
Done.
Now we have all the values we need.
We know distance equals speed multiplied by time.
So distance equals fifteen multiplied by thirty equals four hundred fifty meters. Now that we have found the total distance, we can use it in the next step.
Since length of train plus length of platform equals total distance,
we get two hundred plus x equals four hundred fifty. After simplifying this, we get x equals four hundred fifty minus two hundred, which is two hundred fifty meters. Hence, the length of the
platform is two hundred fifty meter, so the final answer will be option B.
